title: Pure-bridge completion and local exchange
summary: 24 Lean theorems checked: deepest-root convex geometry, conditional exact exchange, and a finite degree-two mark counterexample with costs 1,1,1,2. General graph realization and unrestricted safe cover remain open.

claims.label: Pure-bridge elimination
claims.detail: 4194 finite pure completion instances matched exhaustive source-edge-cut combinations. General graph realization of the exchange interface remains open.

claims.label: Marked role swap and q_J ≤ d_D
claims.detail: 44582 exact finite role swaps; general partition equivalence and target r−1 split construction remain graph obligations.

claims.label: Unrestricted improved exponential bound
claims.detail: No safe-cover lemma; no improvement claimed. Whidden prior-bound audit remains open.

claims.label: Dropping purity fails
claims.detail: Six-leaf counterexample: greedy marking costs 2; exact optimum 1.

claims.label: Separate zero penalties do not compose
claims.detail: Concrete degree-two marks have costs 1,1,1,2. Kernel theorem in the imported RMAF executable model; graph correspondence still open.

lemmas.label: Deepest-root neighborhood
lemmas.detail: Lean theorem for rooted path-convex regions in the binary address tree; graph embeddings must still be shown to realize this structure.

lemmas.label: Free and paid optimum identities
lemmas.detail: Kernel-checked given ExchangeSystem fields, especially one-unit repair of the entire remaining feasible state. No additive-penalty assumption.

lemmas.label: Role-swap optimum and budget arithmetic
lemmas.detail: Kernel-checked for a common feasible partition family with at least r pieces and the supplied h≤d+r−1 bound.

lemmas.label: Finite degree-two synergy
lemmas.detail: All bounded assignments with both marks cost at least two, while either mark alone has optimum one. Shares existing RMAF semantics.

example.caption: Purity-free greedy failure: source is the two-component forest (2,4) and ((0,1),(3,5)); exact refinement has three components (one additional cut), while the greedy extension uses four.
